// File: crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/frame/input.rs (rust)
//! Frame input regions: source-XID-is-truth event targeting.
//!
//! Pure value objects. No X calls, no x11rb.
//!
//! The wm registers each frame child window with its [`FrameRegion`].
//! [`target_for_xid`] looks the source XID up in that registry; a known
//! child keeps its registered region (identity, no geometric re-hit-test).
//! Unknown sources (including the client window) resolve to
//! [`FrameRegion::Client`].

use std::collections::HashMap;

use super::model::{FrameControl, FrameRegion};
use super::resources::FrameEventTarget;

/// Title-button hit target from skin `control_button_geometries`.
/// Hit rects derive from skin geometry; glyph pixels never affect them.
#[must_use]
pub fn frame_control_at(frame_width: u32, titlebar_height: u16, x: i16) -> Option<FrameControl> {
    use super::layout::{
        controls_width_for_titlebar, layout_frame_children, resize_thickness_for_titlebar,
    };
    let width = i32::try_from(frame_width).unwrap_or(i32::MAX);
    let titlebar_h = i32::from(titlebar_height);
    let rects = layout_frame_children(
        width,
        titlebar_h + resize_thickness_for_titlebar(titlebar_h),
        titlebar_h,
        controls_width_for_titlebar(titlebar_h),
        resize_thickness_for_titlebar(titlebar_h),
    )
    .controls;
    let x = i32::from(x);
    if x < 0 || x >= width {
        return None;
    }
    let roles = [
        FrameControl::Minimize,
        FrameControl::MaximizeRestore,
        FrameControl::Close,
    ];
    rects
        .into_iter()
        .zip(roles)
        .find_map(|(rect, role)| (x >= rect.x && x < rect.x + rect.w).then_some(role))
}

/// Resolve an event source XID via the registry map (value-side).
/// Known child XID -> its registered region (source XID is truth, no geometry);
/// anything else -> client.
#[must_use]
pub fn target_for_xid(
    registry: &HashMap<u32, FrameRegion>,
    client: u32,
    source: u32,
) -> FrameEventTarget {
    let region = registry
        .get(&source)
        .copied()
        .unwrap_or(FrameRegion::Client);
    FrameEventTarget { client, region }
}

/// Idle-hover fallback for events whose source XID is not a control child:
/// `frame_control_at` inside the titlebar band, else `None`.
#[must_use]
pub fn frame_control_fallback(
    frame_width: u32,
    titlebar_height: u16,
    x: i16,
    y: i16,
    _current: Option<FrameControl>,
) -> Option<FrameControl> {
    if y < 0 || y >= titlebar_height.max(1) as i16 {
        return None;
    }
    frame_control_at(frame_width, titlebar_height, x)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::frame::coords::{FrameRect, RootPoint, RootRect};
    use crate::frame::model::{FrameControl, ResizeEdges};

    const W: i32 = 400;
    const H: i32 = 300;

    fn test_registry() -> (HashMap<u32, FrameRegion>, u32) {
        let client = 20_u32;
        let mut registry = HashMap::new();
        for (index, edges) in crate::frame::resources::RESIZE_ORDER.iter().enumerate() {
            registry.insert(100 + index as u32, FrameRegion::Resize(*edges));
        }
        registry.insert(200, FrameRegion::TitleDrag);
        registry.insert(201, FrameRegion::Control(FrameControl::Minimize));
        registry.insert(202, FrameRegion::Control(FrameControl::MaximizeRestore));
        registry.insert(203, FrameRegion::Control(FrameControl::Close));
        (registry, client)
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_control_pixel_matches_native_child_at_100_135_200_percent() {
        use crate::frame::layout::{
            controls_width_for_titlebar, layout_frame_children, resize_thickness_for_titlebar,
        };
        for titlebar_h in [31_u16, 42, 62] {
            for width in [100_u32, 160, 400, 800] {
                let height = i32::from(titlebar_h);
                let layout = layout_frame_children(
                    width as i32,
                    300,
                    height,
                    controls_width_for_titlebar(height),
                    resize_thickness_for_titlebar(height),
                );
                for (index, expected) in [
                    FrameControl::Minimize,
                    FrameControl::MaximizeRestore,
                    FrameControl::Close,
                ]
                .into_iter()
                .enumerate()
                {
                    let rect = layout.controls[index];
                    for x in rect.x..rect.x + rect.w {
                        assert_eq!(
                            frame_control_at(width, titlebar_h, x as i16),
                            Some(expected),
                            "width={width} height={height} x={x}"
                        );
                    }
                }
                assert_eq!(frame_control_at(width, titlebar_h, -1), None);
                assert_eq!(frame_control_at(width, titlebar_h, width as i16), None);
                assert_eq!(
                    frame_control_fallback(
                        width,
                        titlebar_h,
                        width as i16 - 1,
                        titlebar_h as i16,
                        None
                    ),
                    None
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_child_is_identity_no_rehittest() {
        let (registry, client) = test_registry();
        // Resize child xid wins even though the "point" conceptually sits
        // elsewhere: no geometric re-hit-test is consulted.
        let target = target_for_xid(&registry, client, 104);
        assert_eq!(
            target,
            FrameEventTarget {
                client,
                region: FrameRegion::Resize(ResizeEdges::top()),
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            target_for_xid(&registry, client, 203).region,
            FrameRegion::Control(FrameControl::Close)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn client_source_is_client_not_resize() {
        let (registry, client) = test_registry();
        // The client xid is not registered as a child: source != resize.
        assert!(!registry.contains_key(&client));
        let target = target_for_xid(&registry, client, client);
        assert_eq!(target.region, FrameRegion::Client);
        assert_eq!(target.client, client);
        // Unknown xid is also client.
        assert_eq!(
            target_for_xid(&registry, client, 9999).region,
            FrameRegion::Client
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn frame_at_root_does_not_change_local_region_result() {
        // Registry resolution is XID-based, so moving the frame outer to
        // root (500,200) cannot change any local region result.
        let origin = RootPoint::new(500, 200);
        let root = RootRect::new(500, 200, W, H);
        let frame = root.to_frame(origin);
        assert_eq!(frame, FrameRect::new(0, 0, W, H));
        let (registry, client) = test_registry();
        let before = target_for_xid(&registry, client, 200);
        let after = target_for_xid(&registry, client, 200);
        assert_eq!(before, after);
        assert_eq!(before.region, FrameRegion::TitleDrag);
        assert_eq!(frame.to_root(origin), root);
    }

    #[test]
    fn eight_resize_zones_unique_via_registry() {
        let (registry, client) = test_registry();
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for xid in 100..108 {
            let target = target_for_xid(&registry, client, xid);
            let seen_key = match target.region {
                FrameRegion::Resize(edges) => (edges.left, edges.right, edges.top, edges.bottom),
                other => panic!("expected resize, got {other:?}"),
            };
            assert!(seen.insert(seen_key), "{seen_key:?} dup");
        }
        assert_eq!(seen.len(), 8);
    }
}


// File: crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/frame/layout.rs (rust)
//! Frame child layout: pure partition of the frame outer into 12 children.
//!
//! Pure value objects. No X calls, no x11rb.
//!
//! J06 freeze: titlebar 31, buttons 3x38x31, controls_width 114,
//! resize thickness 6, min 160x96.
//!
//! Children: 8 resize zones + 1 title-drag body + 3 control buttons.
//! Non-overlap partition (half-open rects):
//! corners 6x6 at outer extremes; top/bottom strips exclude corners
//! (top covers the full width between corners); left/right strips start
//! at `titlebar_h` and exclude corners; title-drag is the titlebar body
//! below the top-6px strip excluding control rects; controls follow the
//! skin formula (`x = W - cw + i*38`, `w = 38`, `h = titlebar_h`) clipped
//! below the top strip when touching it.

use super::coords::FrameRect;
#[cfg(test)]
use super::model::ResizeEdges;

/// Frozen defaults (J06).
pub const TITLEBAR_H: i32 = 31;
/// Three buttons of 38px.
#[cfg(test)]
pub const CONTROLS_WIDTH: i32 = 114;
/// Single button width.
pub const BUTTON_WIDTH: i32 = 38;
/// Resize hit thickness.
pub const RESIZE_T: i32 = 6;

/// Convert authoritative logical control width to the physical titlebar size.
/// The titlebar height is supplied by the frame-extents authority, so hit,
/// glyph, fill and input children derive their scale from the same metric.
#[must_use]
pub fn button_width_for_titlebar(titlebar_h: i32) -> i32 {
    (i64::from(BUTTON_WIDTH) * i64::from(titlebar_h.max(1)) + i64::from(TITLEBAR_H / 2))
        .checked_div(i64::from(TITLEBAR_H))
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .clamp(1, i64::from(i32::MAX)) as i32
}

/// Keep the invisible resize targets proportional to the same titlebar scale.
#[must_use]
pub fn resize_thickness_for_titlebar(titlebar_h: i32) -> i32 {
    (RESIZE_T * titlebar_h.max(1) + TITLEBAR_H / 2) / TITLEBAR_H
}

#[must_use]
pub fn controls_width_for_titlebar(titlebar_h: i32) -> i32 {
    button_width_for_titlebar(titlebar_h).saturating_mul(3)
}

/// Twelve frame children: 8 resize + 1 title-drag + 3 controls.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct FrameChildLayout {
    pub top_left: FrameRect,
    pub top_right: FrameRect,
    pub bottom_left: FrameRect,
    pub bottom_right: FrameRect,
    pub top: FrameRect,
    pub bottom: FrameRect,
    pub left: FrameRect,
    pub right: FrameRect,
    pub title_drag: FrameRect,
    /// Left-to-right: minimize, maximize/restore, close.
    pub controls: [FrameRect; 3],
}

impl FrameChildLayout {
    /// Resize zones paired with their edges, corner-first order.
    #[cfg(test)]
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn resize_pairs() -> [ResizeEdges; 8] {
        crate::frame::resources::RESIZE_ORDER
    }

    /// Resize rects in the same corner-first order as [`Self::resize_pairs`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn resize_rects(self) -> [FrameRect; 8] {
        [
            self.top_left,
            self.top_right,
            self.bottom_left,
            self.bottom_right,
            self.top,
            self.bottom,
            self.left,
            self.right,
        ]
    }
}

/// Pure partition of the frame outer (frame-local origin) into 12 children.
#[must_use]
pub fn layout_frame_children(
    outer_w: i32,
    outer_h: i32,
    titlebar_h: i32,
    controls_width: i32,
    resize_t: i32,
) -> FrameChildLayout {
    let w = outer_w.max(0);
    let h = outer_h.max(0);
    let t = resize_t.max(1);
    let tb = titlebar_h.max(t + 1);
    let cw = controls_width.clamp(0, (w - 2 * t).max(0));
    // Divide the clipped band by thirds without dropping remainder pixels:
    // even the narrowest frame must keep the last Close hit cell flush right.
    let cell_edge = |index: i32| cw.saturating_mul(index) / 3;

    let strip_w = (w - 2 * t).max(0);
    let mid_w = (strip_w - cw).max(0);
    let side_h = (h - tb - t).max(0);

    // Controls from the skin formula, then clipped below the top strip
    // when touching it (control top lives at y=0, strip owns y=0..t).
    let controls = std::array::from_fn(|i| {
        let begin = cell_edge(i as i32);
        let end = cell_edge(i as i32 + 1);
        let raw = FrameRect::new(w - cw + begin, 0, end - begin, tb);
        if raw.y < t {
            FrameRect::new(raw.x, t, raw.w, (raw.h - (t - raw.y)).max(0))
        } else {
            raw
        }
    });

    FrameChildLayout {
        top_left: FrameRect::new(0, 0, t, t),
        top_right: FrameRect::new(w - t, 0, t, t),
        bottom_left: FrameRect::new(0, h - t, t, t),
        bottom_right: FrameRect::new(w - t, h - t, t, t),
        top: FrameRect::new(t, 0, strip_w, t),
        bottom: FrameRect::new(t, h - t, strip_w, t),
        left: FrameRect::new(0, tb, t, side_h),
        right: FrameRect::new(w - t, tb, t, side_h),
        title_drag: FrameRect::new(t, t, mid_w, (tb - t).max(0)),
        controls,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::frame::coords::{RootPoint, RootRect};

    const W: i32 = 400;
    const H: i32 = 300;

    fn layout() -> FrameChildLayout {
        layout_frame_children(W, H, TITLEBAR_H, CONTROLS_WIDTH, RESIZE_T)
    }

    fn overlaps(a: FrameRect, b: FrameRect) -> bool {
        a.x < b.x + b.w && b.x < a.x + a.w && a.y < b.y + b.h && b.y < a.y + a.h
    }

    /// All twelve children: 8 resize, title-drag, 3 controls.
    fn all_children(l: FrameChildLayout) -> Vec<FrameRect> {
        let mut all = l.resize_rects().to_vec();
        all.push(l.title_drag);
        all.extend(l.controls);
        all
    }

    #[test]
    fn j06_zone_pins_400x300() {
        let l = layout();
        assert_eq!(l.top_left, FrameRect::new(0, 0, 6, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.top_right, FrameRect::new(394, 0, 6, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.bottom_left, FrameRect::new(0, 294, 6, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.bottom_right, FrameRect::new(394, 294, 6, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.top, FrameRect::new(6, 0, 388, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.bottom, FrameRect::new(6, 294, 388, 6));
        assert_eq!(l.left, FrameRect::new(0, 31, 6, 263));
        assert_eq!(l.right, FrameRect::new(394, 31, 6, 263));
        assert_eq!(l.title_drag, FrameRect::new(6, 6, 274, 25));
        assert_eq!(
            l.controls,
            [
                FrameRect::new(286, 6, 38, 25),
                FrameRect::new(324, 6, 38, 25),
                FrameRect::new(362, 6, 38, 25),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn top_resize_strip_covers_every_pixel_above_controls() {
        for (w, height) in [(160, 31), (400, 31), (400, 42), (800, 62)] {
            let t = resize_thickness_for_titlebar(height);
            let layout =
                layout_frame_children(w, 300, height, controls_width_for_titlebar(height), t);
            for x in 0..w {
                for y in 0..t {
                    let count = [layout.top_left, layout.top_right, layout.top]
                        .into_iter()
                        .filter(|r| x >= r.x && x < r.x + r.w && y >= r.y && y < r.y + r.h)
                        .count();
                    assert_eq!(count, 1, "x={x} y={y} w={w} height={height}");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn eight_resize_zones_unique() {
        let l = layout();
        let rects = l.resize_rects();
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for rect in rects {
            assert!(rect.w > 0 && rect.h > 0, "{rect:?}");
            assert!(
                seen.insert((rect.x, rect.y, rect.w, rect.h)),
                "{rect:?} dup"
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(seen.len(), 8);
        // Edges pair one-to-one in corner-first order.
        let edges = FrameChildLayout::resize_pairs();
        assert_eq!(
            edges,
            [
                ResizeEdges::top_left(),
                ResizeEdges::top_right(),
                ResizeEdges::bottom_left(),
                ResizeEdges::bottom_right(),
                ResizeEdges::top(),
                ResizeEdges::bottom(),
                ResizeEdges::left(),
                ResizeEdges::right(),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn twelve_children_nonoverlapping() {
        let all = all_children(layout());
        assert_eq!(all.len(), 12);
        for i in 0..all.len() {
            assert!(all[i].w > 0 && all[i].h > 0, "{:?}", all[i]);
            for j in (i + 1)..all.len() {
                assert!(!overlaps(all[i], all[j]), "{:?} vs {:?}", all[i], all[j]);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn title_body_excludes_controls_and_top_resize() {
        let l = layout();
        // Below the top-6px strip, above the titlebar bottom.
        assert!(l.title_drag.y >= RESIZE_T);
        assert_eq!(l.title_drag.y + l.title_drag.h, TITLEBAR_H);
        // Excludes control rects (ends at or before the controls band).
        assert!(l.title_drag.x + l.title_drag.w <= W - CONTROLS_WIDTH);
        assert!(l.title_drag.x + l.title_drag.w <= l.controls[0].x);
        for control in l.controls {
            assert!(!overlaps(l.title_drag, control));
            // Clipped below the top strip.
            assert!(control.y >= RESIZE_T);
            assert!(!overlaps(l.top, control));
        }
        assert!(!overlaps(l.title_drag, l.top));
    }

    #[test]
    fn controls_tile_and_nonoverlap() {
        let l = layout();
        assert_eq!(l.controls[0].w, 38);
        assert_eq!(l.controls[2].x + l.controls[2].w, W);
        assert_eq!(l.controls[0].x + 38, l.controls[1].x);
        assert_eq!(l.controls[1].x + 38, l.controls[2].x);
        assert!(!overlaps(l.controls[0], l.controls[1]));
        assert!(!overlaps(l.controls[1], l.controls[2]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_origin_does_not_change_local_layout() {
        // Layout is frame-local; crossing the (500,200) root origin and back
        // is the identity on every child rect.
        let origin = RootPoint::new(500, 200);
        for rect in all_children(layout()) {
            let root: RootRect = rect.to_root(origin);
            assert_eq!(root.x, rect.x + 500);
            assert_eq!(root.y, rect.y + 200);
            assert_eq!(root.to_frame(origin), rect);
        }
    }

//! Live WM copies of window-behaviour settings, refreshed at the settings sync point.
//!
//! Missing or non-boolean values keep the defaults from `flamewm-platform` settings.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, Ordering};

use flamewm_api::settings::{SettingValue, SettingsSnapshot};
use flamewm_platform::chrome::parse_hex_rgb;

const DEFAULT_SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED: bool = true;
const DEFAULT_FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE: bool = false;
/// XP style: moves and resizes show an outline and apply the real geometry on release.
const DEFAULT_SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING: bool = false;
/// Neutral grey until a settings snapshot supplies `accent`.
const DEFAULT_ACCENT_RGB: (u8, u8, u8) = (0x7f, 0x87, 0x8e);

static SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(DEFAULT_SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED);
static FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(DEFAULT_FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE);
static SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING: AtomicBool =
    AtomicBool::new(DEFAULT_SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING);
/// `shareWallpaper`: one wallpaper spans the outputs instead of one copy per output.
static SHARE_WALLPAPER: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
/// Live `accent` packed as `0x00RRGGBB`.
static ACCENT_RGB: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(pack_rgb(DEFAULT_ACCENT_RGB));

const fn pack_rgb((r, g, b): (u8, u8, u8)) -> u32 {
    ((r as u32) << 16) | ((g as u32) << 8) | b as u32
}

fn boolean_setting(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot, key: &str, default: bool) -> bool {
    match snapshot.values.get(key) {
        Some(SettingValue::Boolean(value)) => *value,
        _ => default,
    }
}

/// Pure mapping from a settings snapshot to `(snapPreviewEnabled, focusFollowsMouse)`.
fn window_behaviour_from_snapshot(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot) -> (bool, bool) {
    (
        boolean_setting(snapshot, "snapPreviewEnabled", DEFAULT_SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED),
        boolean_setting(snapshot, "focusFollowsMouse", DEFAULT_FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE),
    )
}

/// Pure mapping from a settings snapshot to `showContentWhileDragging`.
fn show_content_from_snapshot(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot) -> bool {
    boolean_setting(
        snapshot,
        "showContentWhileDragging",
        DEFAULT_SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING,
    )
}

/// Pure mapping from a settings snapshot to the `defaultTerminal` override; empty when unset.
fn terminal_from_snapshot(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot) -> String {
    match snapshot.values.get("defaultTerminal") {
        Some(SettingValue::Text(value)) => value.clone(),
        _ => String::new(),
    }
}

/// Pure mapping from a settings snapshot to the `accent` colour. Accepts `#RRGGBB` and bare
/// `RRGGBB`, the same forms the shell accepts; invalid or missing values keep the neutral default.
fn accent_from_snapshot(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
    match snapshot.values.get("accent") {
        Some(SettingValue::Text(value)) => {
            parse_hex_rgb(&format!("#{}", value.trim_start_matches('#')))
                .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_ACCENT_RGB)
        }
        _ => DEFAULT_ACCENT_RGB,
    }
}

/// Called from the single settings sync point on the WM thread.
pub(crate) fn sync(snapshot: &SettingsSnapshot) {
    let (snap_preview, focus_follows_mouse) = window_behaviour_from_snapshot(snapshot);
    SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED.store(snap_preview, Ordering::Relaxed);
    FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE.store(focus_follows_mouse, Ordering::Relaxed);
    SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING.store(show_content_from_snapshot(snapshot), Ordering::Relaxed);
    SHARE_WALLPAPER.store(
        boolean_setting(snapshot, "shareWallpaper", false),
        Ordering::Relaxed,
    );
    ACCENT_RGB.store(pack_rgb(accent_from_snapshot(snapshot)), Ordering::Relaxed);
    flamewm_applications::terminal::set_configured_terminal(&terminal_from_snapshot(snapshot));
}

/// Live system accent as `(r, g, b)`; neutral default before the first snapshot.
pub(crate) fn accent_rgb() -> (u8, u8, u8) {
    let packed = ACCENT_RGB.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    ((packed >> 16) as u8, (packed >> 8) as u8, packed as u8)
}

pub(crate) fn snap_preview_enabled() -> bool {
    SNAP_PREVIEW_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

pub(crate) fn focus_follows_mouse() -> bool {
    FOCUS_FOLLOWS_MOUSE.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// `shareWallpaper` (default `false`): whether the desktop shares one wallpaper over all outputs.
pub(crate) fn share_wallpaper() -> bool {
    SHARE_WALLPAPER.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// `false` (default) draws an outline during interactive move/resize.
pub(crate) fn show_content_while_dragging() -> bool {
    SHOW_CONTENT_WHILE_DRAGGING.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod show_content_tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn show_content_defaults_off_and_maps_booleans() {
        assert!(!show_content_from_snapshot(&SettingsSnapshot::new(1)));
        let mut snapshot = SettingsSnapshot::new(1);
        snapshot.values.insert(
            "showContentWhileDragging".into(),
            SettingValue::Boolean(true),
        );
        assert!(show_content_from_snapshot(&snapshot));
        snapshot.values.insert(
            "showContentWhileDragging".into(),
            SettingValue::Text("yes".into()),
        );
        assert!(!show_content_from_snapshot(&snapshot));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn snapshot(entries: &[(&str, SettingValue)]) -> SettingsSnapshot {
        let mut snapshot = SettingsSnapshot::new(1);
        for (key, value) in entries {
            snapshot.values.insert((*key).into(), value.clone());
        }
        snapshot
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_keys_keep_defaults() {
        assert_eq!(
            window_behaviour_from_snapshot(&SettingsSnapshot::new(1)),
            (true, false)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn explicit_booleans_map_directly() {
        let mapped = window_behaviour_from_snapshot(&snapshot(&[
            ("snapPreviewEnabled", SettingValue::Boolean(false)),
            ("focusFollowsMouse", SettingValue::Boolean(true)),
        ]));
        assert_eq!(mapped, (false, true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_terminal_maps_text_and_defaults_empty() {
        assert_eq!(terminal_from_snapshot(&SettingsSnapshot::new(1)), "");
        let configured = snapshot(&[(
            "defaultTerminal",
            SettingValue::Text("kitty".into()),
        )]);
        assert_eq!(terminal_from_snapshot(&configured), "kitty");
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_accent_keeps_neutral_default() {
        assert_eq!(
            accent_from_snapshot(&SettingsSnapshot::new(1)),
            (0x7f, 0x87, 0x8e)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accent_accepts_hash_and_bare_hex() {
        assert_eq!(
            accent_from_snapshot(&snapshot(&[(
                "accent",
                SettingValue::Text("#ef4048".into())
            )])),
            (0xef, 0x40, 0x48)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            accent_from_snapshot(&snapshot(&[(
                "accent",
                SettingValue::Text("123456".into())
            )])),
            (0x12, 0x34, 0x56)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_accent_falls_back_to_neutral_default() {
        assert_eq!(
            accent_from_snapshot(&snapshot(&[(
                "accent",
                SettingValue::Text("#GG0000".into())
            )])),
            (0x7f, 0x87, 0x8e)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_boolean_values_fall_back_to_defaults() {
        let mapped = window_behaviour_from_snapshot(&snapshot(&[
            ("snapPreviewEnabled", SettingValue::Integer(0)),
            ("focusFollowsMouse", SettingValue::Integer(1)),
        ]));
        assert_eq!(mapped, (true, false));
    }
}

128:     /// Applies the minimize end state. `hidden` means the frame was already unmapped

140:                 return Ok(());

138:     /// Apply live chrome tokens from the settings sync point. A change

186:                     hover: state.hover_control,

188:                     maximized: state.is_maximized(),

80:     /// Dispatches a passive-grab KeyPress to the bound action. Only actions
81:     /// with an existing WM path are executed; the rest are logged once.
82:     pub(super) fn handle_key_press(&mut self, event: KeyPressEvent) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
83:         // The raw feed may already have dispatched this key while a client held the keyboard.
84:         if self.raw_claimed(event.time, event.detail) {
85:             return Ok(());
86:         }
87:         let state = u16::from(event.state);
88:         // Passive path while the switcher is open (the raw twin is claimed, so it is skipped).
89:         if self.switcher.is_open() {
90:             self.claim_escape_chord(event.time, event.detail);
91:             return self.switcher_key(event.detail, state);
92:         }
93:         if let Some(active) = self.active {
94:             self.cancel_open_for(active)?;
95:         }
96:         let matched = crate::shortcut_action_for_key(event.detail, state);
97:         if key_diag_enabled() {
98:             eprintln!(
99:                 "flamewm: keypress detail={} state={:04x} action={}",
100:                 event.detail,
101:                 state,
102:                 matched.as_deref().unwrap_or("none")
103:             );
104:         }
105:         if let Some(action) = matched.as_deref().filter(|action| is_escape_chord(action)) {
106:             let action = action.to_owned();
107:             self.claim_escape_chord(event.time, event.detail);
108:             return self.dispatch_escape_chord(&action);
109:         }
110:         // A bare Start-bound Super press only arms the tap; Start toggles on its
111:         // completed release. Any other press completes or cancels a pending tap.
112:         if matched.as_deref() == Some(ACTION_TOGGLE_START_MENU) && is_bare_state(state) {
113:             let outcome = self.super_tap.press_super(event.detail, event.time);
114:             self.apply_super_tap(outcome);
115:             return Ok(());
116:         }
117:         let outcome = self.super_tap.press_other();
118:         self.apply_super_tap(outcome);
119:         let Some(action) = matched else {
120:             return Ok(());
121:         };
122:         match action.as_str() {
123:             ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE => self.on_active(Self::request_close)?,
124:             ACTION_WINDOW_MINIMIZE => self.on_active(Self::minimize)?,
125:             ACTION_WINDOW_MAXIMIZE => self.on_active(Self::toggle_maximize)?,
126:             // Arrow shortcuts follow the product two-row grid: left/right stay inside the
127:             // current row, up/down switch rows, and a missing neighbour is a no-op.
128:             ACTION_WORKSPACE_LEFT
129:             | ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT
130:             | ACTION_WORKSPACE_UP
131:             | ACTION_WORKSPACE_DOWN => {
132:                 if let Some(target) = workspace_shortcut_target(
133:                     self.current_workspace,
134:                     self.workspace_count,
135:                     action.as_str(),
136:                 ) {
137:                     self.switch_workspace(target)?;
138:                 }
139:             }
140:             // Same spawn and supervision path as the Lock session action.
141:             ACTION_OPEN_FILES_SUPER | ACTION_OPEN_FILES_CTRL_ALT => {
142:                 let home = std::env::var_os("HOME")
143:                     .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
144:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from("/"));
145:                 if let Err(error) = std::process::Command::new("xdg-open").arg(home).spawn() {
146:                     eprintln!("flamewm: file explorer shortcut failed: {error}");
147:                 }
148:             }
149:             ACTION_OPEN_TERMINAL_SUPER | ACTION_OPEN_TERMINAL_CTRL_ALT => {
150:                 // The resolver owns the choice: `defaultTerminal` override, else FlameWM Terminal.
151:                 let program = flamewm_applications::terminal::terminal_program();
152:                 if let Err(error) = std::process::Command::new(&program).spawn() {
153:                     eprintln!("flamewm: terminal shortcut failed: {program}: {error}");
154:                 }
155:             }
156:             ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL | ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION | ACTION_SCREENSHOT_WINDOW => {
157:                 // Screenshot runs on demand in its own process; WM input processing must not wait
158:                 // for a region gesture or PNG compression to complete.
159:                 let options: &[&str] = match action.as_str() {
160:                     ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL => &["--full", "--copy"],
161:                     ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION => &["--region", "--annotate", "--copy"],
162:                     _ => &["--active", "--copy"],
163:                 };
164:                 if let Err(error) = std::process::Command::new("flamewm-screenshot")
165:                     .args(options)
166:                     .spawn()
167:                 {
168:                     eprintln!("flamewm: screenshot shortcut failed: {error}");
169:                 }
170:             }
171:             ACTION_SESSION_LOCK => {
172:                 if let Err(error) = flamewm_x11_desktop::start_lock_screen() {
173:                     eprintln!("flamewm: lock shortcut failed: {error:?}");
174:                 }
175:             }
176:             // Chorded start-menu binding: toggle on press. Bare Super is handled above
177:             // and toggles through the SuperTap commit at the end of the batch.
178:             ACTION_TOGGLE_START_MENU => self.changes.start_menu_toggle = true,
179:             ACTION_LAUNCHER => self.changes.launcher_toggle = true,
180:             ACTION_VOLUME_UP => self.changes.media_audio_key = Some(MediaAudioKey::VolumeUp),
181:             ACTION_VOLUME_DOWN => self.changes.media_audio_key = Some(MediaAudioKey::VolumeDown),
182:             ACTION_VOLUME_MUTE => self.changes.media_audio_key = Some(MediaAudioKey::VolumeMute),
183:             other => log_unhandled_shortcut_once(other),
184:         }
185:         Ok(())
186:     }

205:     /// Takes every fullscreen client out of fullscreen and iconifies it, so the desktop is
206:     /// reachable. When another client still owns the keyboard, it is also asked to close.
207:     pub(super) fn break_fullscreen_trap(&mut self) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
208:         let targets = self.fullscreen_clients();
209:         for &client in &targets {
210:             self.set_fullscreen(client, false)?;
211:             self.minimize(client)?;
212:         }
213:         if !targets.is_empty() && self.keyboard_grabbed_by_other()? {
214:             for &client in &targets {
215:                 self.close(client)?;
216:             }
217:         }
218:         Ok(())
219:     }

221:     /// Ctrl+Alt+Escape. The first press breaks the fullscreen client out and asks it to close.
222:     /// A second press within the window kills it when it still owns the keyboard.
223:     fn fullscreen_escape(&mut self) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
224:         if let Some((client, since)) = self.escape_pending.take() {
225:             if since.elapsed() < ESCAPE_KILL_WINDOW
226:                 && self.clients.contains_key(&client)
227:                 && self.keyboard_grabbed_by_other()?
228:             {
229:                 self.conn.kill_client(client)?;
230:                 return Ok(());
231:             }
232:         }
233:         let Some(&client) = self.fullscreen_clients().first() else {
234:             return Ok(());
235:         };
236:         self.escape_pending = Some((client, std::time::Instant::now()));
237:         self.break_fullscreen_trap()
238:     }

242:     fn switch_window(&mut self) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
243:         let tree = self.conn.query_tree(self.screen().root)?.reply()?;
244:         // `children` is bottom-to-top; walk it topmost-first.
245:         let stack: Vec<Window> = tree
246:             .children
247:             .iter()
248:             .rev()
249:             .filter_map(|frame| self.frame_to_client.get(frame).copied())
250:             .collect();

252:             self.clients.get(&client).is_some_and(|state| {
253:                 state.kind == WindowKind::Normal && state.visible_on(self.current_workspace)

255:         });
256:         match target {
257:             Some(client) => self.focus(client),
258:             None => Ok(()),
259:         }
260:     }

262:     pub(super) fn move_to_workspace(
263:         &mut self,
264:         client: Window,
265:         target: usize,
266:     ) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
267:         if target >= self.workspace_count {
268:             return Ok(());
269:         }
270:         self.snap_preview.hide();
271:         let (frame, was_visible, visible) = {
272:             let Some(state) = self.clients.get_mut(&client) else {
273:                 return Ok(());
274:             };
275:             let was_visible = state.visible_on(self.current_workspace);
276:             state.workspace = target;
277:             (
278:                 state.frame,
279:                 was_visible,
280:                 state.visible_on(self.current_workspace),
281:             )
282:         };
283:         self.set_client_workspace(client, target)?;
284:         // A window moved out of the active workspace cannot remain the
285:         // EWMH active window. Clear its old focus-restoration slot too, or
286:         // switching back can try to refocus a window that now lives elsewhere.
287:         if !visible && self.active == Some(client) {
288:             self.active = None;
289:             if let Some(slot) = self.workspace_focus.get_mut(self.current_workspace) {
290:                 if *slot == Some(client) {
291:                     *slot = None;
292:                 }
293:             }
294:             self.publish_active()?;
295:         }
296:         self.mark_windows();
297:         self.mark_workspaces();
298:         // A minimized window or a window moved between two inactive
299:         // workspaces remains unmapped. Issuing another unmap would increment
300:         // ignore_unmap without a corresponding UnmapNotify and could later
301:         // suppress a genuine client withdrawal.
302:         if let Some(should_map) = frame_visibility_delta(was_visible, visible) {
303:             if should_map {
304:                 self.conn.map_window(frame)?;
305:             } else {
306:                 if let Some(state) = self.clients.get_mut(&client) {
307:                     state.ignore_unmap = state.ignore_unmap.saturating_add(1);
308:                 }
309:                 self.conn.unmap_window(frame)?;
310:             }
311:         }
312:         Ok(())
313:     }

// File: crates/flamewm-api/src/shortcuts.rs (rust)
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub const ACTION_TOGGLE_START_MENU: &str = "ToggleStartMenu";
pub const ACTION_LAUNCHER: &str = "Launcher";
pub const ACTION_WORKSPACE_LEFT: &str = "WorkspaceLeft";
pub const ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT: &str = "WorkspaceRight";
pub const ACTION_WORKSPACE_UP: &str = "WorkspaceUp";
pub const ACTION_WORKSPACE_DOWN: &str = "WorkspaceDown";

pub const ACTION_WINDOW_SWITCH: &str = "WindowSwitch";
pub const ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP: &str = "ShowDesktop";
pub const ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP_CTRL_ALT: &str = "ShowDesktopCtrlAlt";
pub const ACTION_FULLSCREEN_ESCAPE: &str = "FullscreenEscape";
pub const ACTION_SESSION_LOCK: &str = "SessionLock";
pub const ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL: &str = "ScreenshotFull";
pub const ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION: &str = "ScreenshotRegion";
pub const ACTION_SCREENSHOT_WINDOW: &str = "ScreenshotWindow";

/// Direction a workspace navigation shortcut moves in the two-row topology, or `None` for any
/// other action. The grid itself lives in [`crate::workspace`].
#[must_use]
pub fn workspace_direction(action: &str) -> Option<crate::workspace::GridDirection> {
    match action {
        ACTION_WORKSPACE_LEFT => Some(crate::workspace::GridDirection::Left),
        ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT => Some(crate::workspace::GridDirection::Right),
        ACTION_WORKSPACE_UP => Some(crate::workspace::GridDirection::Up),
        ACTION_WORKSPACE_DOWN => Some(crate::workspace::GridDirection::Down),
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KeyBinding(pub Option<String>);

impl KeyBinding {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn assigned(value: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let value = value.into();
        Self((!value.is_empty()).then_some(value))
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub const fn unassigned() -> Self {
        Self(None)
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_assigned(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_some()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ShortcutSnapshot {
    pub revision: u64,
    pub bindings: BTreeMap<String, KeyBinding>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ShortcutRegistry {
    bindings: BTreeMap<String, KeyBinding>,
    defaults: BTreeMap<String, KeyBinding>,
}

impl Default for ShortcutRegistry {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let defaults = BTreeMap::from([
            (
                ACTION_TOGGLE_START_MENU.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Super_L"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_WORKSPACE_LEFT.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Left"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Right"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_WORKSPACE_UP.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Up"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_WORKSPACE_DOWN.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Down"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Alt+F4"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Print"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Shift+Print"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_SCREENSHOT_WINDOW.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Print"),
            ),
            (ACTION_WINDOW_MINIMIZE.to_owned(), KeyBinding::unassigned()),
            (ACTION_WINDOW_MAXIMIZE.to_owned(), KeyBinding::unassigned()),
            (
                ACTION_WINDOW_SWITCH.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Alt+Tab"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Super+d"),
            ),
            (

            ),

            ),
            (
                ACTION_LAUNCHER.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Super+space"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_OPEN_FILES_SUPER.to_owned(),
                KeyBinding::assigned("Super+E"),
            ),
            (

                KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Alt+E"),
            ),
            (
                ACTION_OPEN_TERMINAL_SUPER.to_owned(),

        Self {

}

impl ShortcutRegistry {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn bindings(&self) -> &BTreeMap<String, KeyBinding> {
        &self.bindings
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn binding(&self, action: &str) -> Option<&KeyBinding> {
        self.bindings.get(action)
    }

    pub fn clear(&mut self, action: &str) -> FlameResult<()> {
        self.require_action(action)?;
        self.bindings
            .insert(action.to_owned(), KeyBinding::unassigned());
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn reset_one(&mut self, action: &str) -> FlameResult<()> {
        let default = self
            .defaults
            .get(action)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| FlameError::new(ErrorCode::NotFound, "unknown shortcut action"))?;
        self.bindings.insert(action.to_owned(), default);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn set(&mut self, action: &str, raw: &str) -> FlameResult<()> {
        self.require_action(action)?;
        let Some(normalized) = checked_binding(action, raw)? else {
            return self.clear(action);
        };
        // The key moves to `action`: a binding owns one key, so the previous owner is unassigned.
        while let Some(previous) = self.conflict_for(action, &normalized) {
            self.bindings.insert(previous, KeyBinding::unassigned());
        }
        self.bindings
            .insert(action.to_owned(), KeyBinding::assigned(normalized));
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn replace_all(&mut self, desired: &BTreeMap<String, KeyBinding>) -> FlameResult<()> {
        for action in desired.keys() {
            self.require_action(action)?;
        }

        let mut candidate = BTreeMap::new();
        for action in ACTIONS {
            let binding = match desired.get(action).and_then(|binding| binding.0.as_deref()) {
                Some(raw) => checked_binding(action, raw)?
                    .map_or_else(KeyBinding::unassigned, KeyBinding::assigned),
                None => KeyBinding::unassigned(),
            };
            candidate.insert(action.to_owned(), binding);
        }

        // Duplicates never fail the set: the first action (registry order) keeps the key.
        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for binding in candidate.values_mut() {
            if binding
                .0
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|v| !seen.insert(v.to_ascii_lowercase()))
            {
                *binding = KeyBinding::unassigned();
            }
        }

        self.bindings = candidate;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn conflict_for(&self, action: &str, normalized: &str) -> Option<String> {
        self.bindings.iter().find_map(|(other_action, binding)| {
            if other_action == action {
                return None;
            }
            binding.0.as_ref().and_then(|value| {
                (normalize(value).eq_ignore_ascii_case(normalized)).then(|| other_action.clone())
            })
        })
    }

    fn require_action(&self, action: &str) -> FlameResult<()> {
        if ACTIONS.contains(&action) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(FlameError::new(
                ErrorCode::NotFound,
                format!("unknown shortcut action: {action}"),
            ))
        }
    }
}

#[must_use]
pub fn normalize(raw: &str) -> String {
    raw.trim()
        .split('+')
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|part| !part.is_empty())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("+")
}

/// Normalizes and validates a raw binding; `None` means the action is cleared.
fn checked_binding(action: &str, raw: &str) -> FlameResult<Option<String>> {
    let normalized = normalize(raw);
    if normalized.is_empty() || normalized.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Escape") {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    validate_binding(&normalized)?;
    if is_modifier_only(&normalized) && action != ACTION_TOGGLE_START_MENU {
        return Err(FlameError::new(
            ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
            "modifier-only binding is permitted only for ToggleStartMenu",
        ));
    }
    if is_bare_typing_key(&normalized) {
        return Err(FlameError::new(
            ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
            "a single letter or digit needs Ctrl, Alt or Super: bound bare it would fire while typing",
        ));
    }
    Ok(Some(normalized))
}

/// True for a binding whose key is one printable character bound without Ctrl, Alt or Super.
/// Such a binding grabs an ordinary typing key: `d` would toggle its action on every keystroke.
/// Shift does not count (Shift+d is how you type `D`), and bare modifier keys ("Super") are
/// not typing keys and are handled by [`is_modifier_only`].
#[must_use]
pub fn is_bare_typing_key(normalized: &str) -> bool {
    let tokens: Vec<&str> = normalized.split('+').map(str::trim).collect();
    let Some((key, prefix)) = tokens.split_last() else {
        return false;
    };
    let mut chars = key.chars();
    let single =
        matches!(chars.next(), Some(only) if only.is_ascii_graphic()) && chars.next().is_none();
    single
        && !prefix.iter().any(|token| {
            matches!(
                token.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),
                "ctrl" | "control" | "alt" | "super" | "meta" | "win" | "logo" | "hyper"
            )
        })
}

pub fn validate_binding(normalized: &str) -> FlameResult<()> {
    if normalized.len() > 64 || normalized.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        return Err(FlameError::new(
            ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
            "shortcut binding is invalid",
        ));
    }
    if normalized.split('+').any(str::is_empty) {
        return Err(FlameError::new(
            ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
            "shortcut contains an empty token",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[must_use]
pub fn is_modifier_only(normalized: &str) -> bool {
    normalized.split('+').all(|token| {
        matches!(
            token.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),
            "ctrl" | "shift" | "alt" | "super" | "meta" | "hyper" | "super_l" | "super_r"
        )
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

    #[test]
    fn launcher_is_a_registered_action_with_super_space_default() {
        assert_eq!(ACTIONS.len(), 24);
        assert!(ACTIONS.contains(&ACTION_LAUNCHER));
        let defaults = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        assert_eq!(
            defaults.binding(ACTION_LAUNCHER),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Super+space"))
        );
    }
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn escape_clears_binding_instead_of_becoming_a_binding() {
        let mut registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        registry
            .set(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE, "Escape")
            .expect("Escape means clear");
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE),
            Some(&KeyBinding::unassigned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_binding_moves_the_key_to_the_new_action() {
        let mut registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        registry
            .set(ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT, "Ctrl+Super+Left")
            .expect("duplicate takes the key over");
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_WORKSPACE_RIGHT),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Left"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_WORKSPACE_LEFT),
            Some(&KeyBinding::unassigned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_lock_defaults_to_super_l_and_conflicts_with_other_actions() {
        let mut registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Super+L"))
        );
        assert!(ACTIONS.contains(&ACTION_SESSION_LOCK));
        registry
            .set(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE, "super+l")
            .expect("Super+L moves from the lock action");
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK),
            Some(&KeyBinding::unassigned())
        );
        registry
            .set(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK, "Ctrl+Super+K")
            .expect("lock can be rebound");
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+K"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn config_without_session_lock_key_loads_the_default_lock_binding() {
        // A settings file written before SessionLock existed has no hotkey.SessionLock entry.
        let persisted =
            BTreeMap::from([(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE.to_owned(), "Ctrl+Super+Q".to_owned())]);
        let effective = crate::services::shortcuts::effective_registry(&persisted)
            .expect("legacy config is valid");
        assert_eq!(
            effective.binding(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Super+L"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            effective.binding(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Super+Q"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn screenshot_shortcuts_are_three_independent_configurable_actions() {
        let mut registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        for (action, binding) in [
            (ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL, "Print"),
            (ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION, "Shift+Print"),
            (ACTION_SCREENSHOT_WINDOW, "Ctrl+Print"),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                registry.binding(action),
                Some(&KeyBinding::assigned(binding))
            );
            assert!(ACTIONS.contains(&action));
        }
        assert_eq!(
            registry.conflict_for(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION, "Print"),
            Some(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_FULL.to_owned())
        );
        registry.clear(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION),
            Some(&KeyBinding::unassigned())
        );
        registry.reset_one(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SCREENSHOT_REGION),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Shift+Print"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn media_keys_default_to_xf86_bindings_without_changing_existing_defaults() {
        let registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_VOLUME_UP),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("XF86AudioRaiseVolume"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_VOLUME_DOWN),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("XF86AudioLowerVolume"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_VOLUME_MUTE),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("XF86AudioMute"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SESSION_LOCK),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Super+L"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_WINDOW_CLOSE),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Alt+F4"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bare_letter_or_digit_binding_is_rejected() {
        let mut registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        for binding in ["d", "D", "5", "Shift+q", "Shift+D"] {
            assert!(
                is_bare_typing_key(&normalize(binding)),
                "{binding} must be recognised as a typing key"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                registry
                    .set(ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP, binding)
                    .expect_err("a bare typing key must be rejected")
                    .code,
                ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
                "{binding}"
            );
        }
        // The chords and the modifier-only start binding stay valid.
        for binding in ["Super+d", "Ctrl+Alt+d", "Ctrl+Super+Left", "XF86AudioMute"] {
            assert!(!is_bare_typing_key(&normalize(binding)), "{binding}");
        }
        registry
            .set(ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP, "Super+d")
            .expect("Super+d is valid");
        // A persisted set that lost its modifier is refused as a whole, so the WM grabs the
        // defaults instead of installing a bare-`d` grab.
        let persisted = BTreeMap::from([(ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP.to_owned(), "d".to_owned())]);
        let error = crate::services::shortcuts::effective_registry(&persisted)
            .expect_err("a persisted bare letter must not load");
        assert_eq!(error.code, ErrorCode::InvalidArgument);
    }

    #[test]
    fn show_desktop_defaults_keep_both_explicit_chords() {
        let registry = ShortcutRegistry::default();
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Super+d"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            registry.binding(ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP_CTRL_ALT),
            Some(&KeyBinding::assigned("Ctrl+Alt+d"))
        );
        assert!(ACTIONS.contains(&ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP));
        assert!(ACTIONS.contains(&ACTION_SHOW_DESKTOP_CTRL_ALT));
        // Both bindings resolve to their own action, so neither is unassigned by a conflict.
        let effective = crate::services::shortcuts::effective_registry(&BTreeMap::new())
            .expect("defaults are valid");
        assert_eq!(effective, registry);
    }
}

104: /// Rows in the product workspace topology.
105: ///
106: /// Every workspace count is laid out on exactly two rows; the column count follows the live
107: /// workspace count, so four workspaces read `1 2 / 3 4` and six read `1 2 3 / 4 5 6`. Left/right
108: /// stay inside the current row, up/down switch rows. This module is the single owner of that
109: /// grid: the WM resolves arrow shortcuts with it, the shell pager renders with it, and the
110: /// `_NET_DESKTOP_VIEWPORT` publication exposes it to external EWMH pagers.
111: pub const WORKSPACE_ROWS: usize = 2;
112: 
113: /// Columns the two-row topology needs for `count` workspaces (`ceil(count / 2)`, at least 1).
114: #[must_use]
115: pub fn workspace_columns(count: usize) -> usize {
116:     if count == 0 {
117:         1
118:     } else {
119:         count.div_ceil(WORKSPACE_ROWS)
120:     }
121: }
122: 
123: /// Cell of the two-row topology.
124: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
125: pub struct GridPosition {
126:     pub row: usize,
127:     pub column: usize,
128: }
129: 
130: /// Row-major cell of `index`; `None` when `index` is outside `count`.
131: #[must_use]
132: pub fn grid_position(index: usize, count: usize) -> Option<GridPosition> {
133:     if index >= count {
134:         return None;
135:     }
136:     let columns = workspace_columns(count);
137:     Some(GridPosition {
138:         row: index / columns,
139:         column: index % columns,
140:     })
141: }
142: 
143: /// Absolute index of cell `(row, column)`; `None` for a row outside the topology or an empty cell
144: /// (the lower row of a column that only holds an upper workspace).
145: #[must_use]
146: pub fn grid_index(row: usize, column: usize, count: usize) -> Option<usize> {
147:     if row >= WORKSPACE_ROWS || column >= workspace_columns(count) {
148:         return None;
149:     }

100: pub fn keysym_for_name(name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
101:     let mut chars = name.chars();
102:     let single = chars.next().filter(|_| chars.next().is_none());
103:     if let Some(only) = single.filter(char::is_ascii_alphanumeric) {
104:         return Some(u32::from(only.to_ascii_lowercase()));

106:     KEYSYM_NAMES
107:         .iter()
108:         .find(|(known, _)| known.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
109:         .map(|(_, keysym)| *keysym)

111:             // Round-trips keys the capture UI has no name for: `Keysym(0x1008ff18)`.
112:             let hex = name.strip_prefix("Keysym(0x")?.strip_suffix(')')?;
113:             u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok().filter(|k| *k != 0)
114:         })
115: }

198	    /// Hyprland-style binds whose target is encoded in the action id: absolute workspace
199	    /// activation/move and directional focus/move. Returns false for any other action.
200	    fn dispatch_hyprland_binding(&mut self, action: &str) -> Result<bool, ReplyError> {
201	        if let Some(index) = workspace_activate_index(action) {
202	            if index < self.workspace_count {
203	                self.switch_workspace(index)?;
204	            }
205	            return Ok(true);
206	        }
207	        if let Some(index) = workspace_move_index(action) {
208	            if index < self.workspace_count {
209	                if let Some(client) = self.active {
210	                    self.move_to_workspace(client, index)?;
211	                }
212	            }
213	            return Ok(true);
214	        }
215	        if let Some(direction) = focus_direction(action) {
216	            self.focus_direction(direction)?;
217	            return Ok(true);
218	        }

261	    /// Toggle fullscreen from a keybind (`Super+F`). Unlike `FullscreenEscape`, this is a
262	    /// reversible toggle and never kills the client.
263	    pub(super) fn toggle_fullscreen(&mut self, client: Window) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
264	        let fullscreen = self
265	            .clients
266	            .get(&client)
267	            .is_some_and(|state| state.is_fullscreen());
268	        self.set_fullscreen(client, !fullscreen)
269	    }
270	
271	    /// `Super+V`: floating becomes the work-area fill ("pseudo-tile"), anything else returns
272	    /// to the remembered floating rect. There is no tiling engine to toggle against.
273	    pub(super) fn toggle_float(&mut self, client: Window) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
274	        match self
275	            .clients
276	            .get(&client)
277	            .map(|state| state.placement.mode)
278	        {
279	            Some(PlacementMode::Floating) => self.toggle_maximize(client),
280	            Some(_) => self.return_to_floating(client),
281	            None => Ok(()),
282	        }
283	    }
284	
285	    /// Leaves snap/maximize/fullscreen at the floating restore rect, without a pointer drag.
286	    pub(super) fn return_to_floating(&mut self, client: Window) -> Result<(), ReplyError> {
287	        let Some(state) = self.clients.get_mut(&client) else {
288	            return Ok(());
289	        };
290	        let restore = state.placement.floating_restore;
291	        state.placement.mode = PlacementMode::Floating;
292	        state.placement.current = restore;
293	        state.placement.resume = None;
294	        state.set_outer(restore.to_legacy());
295	        self.apply_frame_geometry(client)?;
296	        self.layout_input_children(client)?;
297	        self.paint_chrome(client)?;

+/// Window buttons `#task-slots` renders: `taskbarActivities` off hides the whole area.
+pub(crate) fn task_slots_rendered(states: usize, items: TaskbarItems) -> usize {

+pub(crate) fn project_task_slots_extent(

+        TASKBAR_ELEMENT_HEIGHT,
