> ❯ # FlameWM: Eliminate Xorg CPU saturation during desktop rubber-band selection
>
> **Type:** one self-contained implementation handoff for the next coding-agent session.  
> **Priority:** implement after the agent's current in-flight feature work; do not interrupt, reset, or overwrite it.  
> **Reference baseline:** source archive `2111_25_10_26.tar.gz` (25 Oct 2026); session history `command-code-session-d43359ce.md`. **Use the agent's current working tree as the implementation authority**; re-read affected code because it may have changed since the archive.  
> **Platform:** native FlameWM **X11**, not the Wayland backend.  
> **Goal:** dragging an empty-desktop selection rectangle at high mouse polling rates must remain visually identical but impose *minimal* Xorg and desktop/WM CPU, bounded by the pixels that visibly change, not by full-screen pixels or the rectangle's accumulated interior. No work while stationary.
>
> ## Non-negotiable outcomes
>
> 1. No full desktop wallpaper/icon scene repaint per `MotionNotify` for a pure rubber-band drag. Updates repaint only newly changed screen pixels, including old/new borders and selected/unselected icon tiles. Ensure **bounded dirty area**, not an expanding rectangle union.
> 2. No CPU recomposition or `PutImage` for an entire overlapping frame-shadow region on every mouse movement. Shadow composition must touch only **actual changed coverage**, including transitions between 1–2px border and translucent fill. Non-intersecting shadows receive **zero** X drawing requests.
> 3. Do not make synchronous `get_property(...).reply()` round trips for every queued `_FLAMEWM_RUBBER` notification when the WM can process just the newest state for one display turn. Process release/clear promptly.
> 4. Preserve the exact current style/behavior: selection opacity setting and accent colors, border, dimensions and coordinate transform, icon highlighting, input transparency/hit testing, Z order relative to desktop icons and floating notes/context menus, active work area per output, negative/leftward/upward drags, snaps, drag threshold, release cleanup, shadows above the band, and scale/resize/Expose behavior.
> 5. Never replace the visual with a temporary wireframe, opaque rectangle, XOR artifact, a flashing window, or an overlay that captures mouse input. No disabling window shadows or selecting fewer items as a shortcut.
> 6. A zero-CPU **idle** result is required; absolute 0% CPU during active drawing is physically impossible. Measure and minimize active cost for **Xorg/Xephyr and FlameWM processes separately**, not just the renderer PID. Do not claim a performance win without release-binary before/after evidence on equivalent workloads.
> 7. No global activation of experimental `FLAMEWM_RENDER_REGION=1`, no broad renderer refactor, no new GPU requirement, no per-event allocations proportional to viewport or old rectangle area, and no new long-running polling/animation loop.
>
> ## What source inspection has established (not a live performance measurement)
>
> ### A. Selection event → document mutation → WM property storm
>
> - `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/main.rs`, `handle_surface` around lines **1545–1605**: `UiActionPhase::Motion` computes `normalized_selection_rect`, executes `apply_rubber_hits`, and calls `set_selection_overlay` on every changed geometry. Press/release and work-area clamping are here. Keep semantics and event ordering.
> - `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/rubber.rs`, `set_selection_overlay` around **147–168**: the desktop mutates visibility/position/size on `desktop-selection` through `UiDocumentAccess`, then calls `publish_root_rubber`. `apply_rubber_hits` already uses a frozen list (`rubber_snapshot`) and diff-only item toggles; **do not regress those optimizations**.
> - `crates/flamewm-ui-x11/src/root_property.rs`, `RootCardinalPublisher::set`: every changed rectangle calls X11 `change_property32` and `flush()` (or delete on release) over an **independent** X11 connection.
> - `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/events.rs`, `Event::PropertyNotify` around **55–62**: every `_FLAMEWM_RUBBER` event invokes `on_root_rubber_changed`.
> - `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/shadow.rs`, `on_root_rubber_changed` around **460–495**: a **synchronous** `get_property(...).reply()` for each event, followed by a recomposition and upload for every intersecting frame shadow. Coalescing events in the desktop's own X connection does not automatically coalesce the WM's separate connection.
>
> ### B. The current shadow damage rectangle is far too coarse
>
> - `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/frame/shadow_rubber.rs`, `damage_region`: computes the *bounding union* of the **entire old and new rubber rectangle intersections** with the shadow. Even if only the outer edge moves 2 pixels, a wide previously painted translucent interior may be recomposed again. `compose_region` visits every pixel in this union.
> - `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/shadow.rs`, `put_shadow_region`: creates/frees a GC on every update, chunks a CPU `Vec<u8>` into `put_image` requests, then calls `clear_area` to display the changed shadow pixmap. Full-area image uploads and server-side copies are primary **architectural candidates** for the observed Xorg saturation. For illustration only, a 1920×1080 32-bit region transfers ~7.9 MiB **per update per shadow**; 100 such updates approach ~791 MiB of pixel payload without accounting for actual clipping. Confirm real dimensions and request counts before citing real bandwidth.
> - `crates/flamewm-api/src/root_rubber.rs` owns the six-CARDINAL protocol and `ROOT_RUBBER_BORDER_PX = 2`, while `ui/desktop/desktop.css` declares a 1px selection border. Preserve **currently rendered visible pixels**; verify the two representations before touching border math rather than silently "correcting" either.
> - Current cached unshaded `FrameShadow.raw` and server `FrameShadow.pixmap` are useful; reuse them. No root `GetImage` or server grab is necessary during the active gesture.
>
> ### C. Default X11 rendering paints the entire desktop window
>
> - `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/mod.rs`, `region_paint` initialization around **629–630**: `FLAMEWM_RENDER_REGION=1` is **opt-in**; default is false.
> - `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/damage_plan.rs` explicitly documents correctness failures from enabling the generic region renderer globally; `plan_region_paint` returns `Full` with `region_disabled`, `region_too_large`, and other fallback reasons.
> - `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/render.rs`, `redraw` around **200–335**: rebuilds/compares paint commands, chooses a plan, then `paint_full` clears, redraws the desktop wallpaper, content and selection, and `present_scene` copies the full window. An overlay geometry mutation is real document damage, so it cannot use the interaction-only `Skip` path. `refresh_shape_mask_from_coverage_scaled` also runs for every changed redraw; its server update may be cached, but its coverage computation still merits profiling.
> - `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/events.rs`, `MOTION_NOTIFY` around **465–564** already coalesces **contiguous, same-window** motion without crossing release events. Preserve this ordering. This is not sufficient to eliminate a full repaint on each delivered motion.
> - `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/region_equivalence_tests.rs` already contains `selection_overlay_drag_full_vs_region_timing` and pixel-equivalence machinery. Extend it to cover the **real desktop selection** and the new default-on specialized path.
> - `ui/desktop/index.html` owns `desktop-selection`, `ui/desktop/desktop.css` owns `.selection`; `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/projection.rs` assigns its `UiLayer::Selection`, above content and below popovers. A native child/override-redirect window is **not automatically compatible** with this Z-order or click-through requirement. Avoid creating one unless exact hierarchy/input/stacking equivalence is proven.
>
> **Evidence classification:** these are demonstrable control-flow/cost problems in the attached source. Which dominates the user's actual Xorg CPU **has not been proven by profiling this machine**. Implement instrumentation to distinguish the two rather than calling either a measured 100% root cause.
>
> ## Required implementation sequence
>
> ### 0. Protect current work; capture a trustworthy baseline
>
> Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `docs/CANONICAL_OWNERS.md`, and the **current** agent governance files if present; follow active source/version rules. Do not run `git reset --hard`, force checkout, modify unrelated features, or overwrite files that the current feature agent is editing. Work from the current post-feature state. Identify and report the exact `git rev-parse HEAD` and git diff state when starting.
>
> Use a dedicated nested Xephyr/X11 display with isolated session bus (`scripts/xephyr`), plus a real Xorg session verification if a safe test environment is available. **Never use `DISPLAY=:0` as a test target by assumption**. Build release for both baseline and candidate, same compiler/profile, monitor, resolution, desktop icons, Xorg/Xephyr server and hardware acceleration mode. Record 3–5 runs, medians and variations. Keep browser/other builds off during profiling when possible.
>
> Measure for a repeatable gesture set: (1) 10s idle, (2) mouse motion with no button, (3) slow drag 300 px, (4) fast drag over 1500+ px, (5) drag through floating-window shadows, (6) drag through 50+ desktop icons, (7) shift to all four directions / cross-output bounds where supported, (8) release and idle again. Repro must include mouse-motion throughput and the number of actual present frames, not just elapsed drag seconds.
>
> In builds with temporary debug-only counters, aggregate without logging per motion:
>
> ```text
> input.motion_seen / input.motion_coalesced
> selection.overlay_changes / selection.item_toggle_count
> render.plan_full / render.plan_region / render.plan_skip
> render.copied_px / render.paint_visits / render.shape_calls
> wm.rubber_property_events / wm.rubber_property_reads / wm.rubber_states_applied
> wm.rubber_shadow_regions / wm.rubber_put_image_calls / wm.rubber_uploaded_bytes
> wm.rubber_affected_pixels / wm.rubber_non_intersecting_shadows
> ```
>
> Add counters to the **owners** shown above. Distinguish X11 request bytes/affected pixels from CPU memory copies and `Xorg` CPU. Existing `FLAMEWM_PROFILE=1`, `FLAMEWM_PROFILE_INTERVAL`, `FLAMEWM_PROFILE_DIR`, `FLAMEWM_DEBUG_PLAN` are useful for diagnosis; leave verbose/debug instrumentation disabled by default. Measure system server with `pidstat -u -p <Xorg-or-Xephyr-pid> 1` if available; optional `perf record -g -p <pid> -- sleep 10` when permitted. Avoid unrelated system changes or privilege tweaks to obtain perf access.
>
> ### 1. Fix shadow recomposition FIRST: exact narrow damage strips, not the old/new union
>
> **Owner:** `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/frame/shadow_rubber.rs`; integrated caller `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/shadow.rs`.
>
> Replace `damage_region() -> Option<Rect>` **in the active rubber update pipeline** with an exact (or conservatively small) **set of non-overlapping dirty rectangles**. For every screen pixel `p`:
>
> ```text
> old_color(p) = old.and_then(|r| rubber_coverage(r, p))
> new_color(p) = new.and_then(|r| rubber_coverage(r, p))
> dirty(p) = old_color(p) != new_color(p)
> ```
>
> This equality is the definition of the *rubber coverage difference*. It must include old/new border bands and fill-alpha/color edits, handle signs, expand/shrink from each corner, changes in transparency, complete removal, and clip to each cached shadow extent. Implement a bounded small-rectangle decomposition using old/new left/right/top/bottom boundaries plus border-width offsets, coalescing adjacent cells of equal classification; a scan over **only coordinate breakpoints** is acceptable, a scan of the full expanded rectangle is not. Allow a small optional 1–2 pixel anti-aliasing pad only where the actual renderer needs it. If damage cells are too fragmented, choose a cost-based fallback, but never routinely regress a 2px edge move to a full 1000×800 recomposition.
>
> `compose_region` can remain the pure pixel-reference implementation for each small region. Feed each region separately to `put_shadow_region`. Reuse GC(s) rather than create/free per motion, with explicit teardown when shadows are removed. If `put_image` cost remains high, consider a **server-side** equivalent that preserves existing `keep_at` shadow gradient and per-pixel alpha; do not substitute a uniform shadow. No X11 round trip, get_image, heap image sized to entire rubber band, or root server grab during an active motion.
>
> If there are no floating windows, no frame shadows, or no overlapping **changed coverage**, expect **zero** shadow drawing requests. On release, restore exact unmodified shadow pixels only where coverage actually changed. Preserve shadow stacking, focus-dependent gradient, `ShadowScene` generation/deferred reshadings, and existing frame movement/resize behavior.
>
> ### 2. Coalesce the WM's cross-process property notifications correctly
>
> **Owners:** `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/events.rs`, `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/shadow.rs`; publisher `crates/flamewm-ui-x11/src/root_property.rs` only if measurement warrants it.
>
> Mark rubber updates **pending** when receiving the correct atom/window; after draining the current event batch in the existing WM reactor, query the latest six-cardinal property **once** and process the newest state, with no extra event loop, no timer when idle and no delay beyond the next render turn. Verify placement in the **actual WM reactor**; do not introduce code that never runs or that starves while mouse events keep arriving.
>
> Avoid queuing a million intermediate shadow renders for stale positions. Do not merge past a semantic release/clear without ensuring the final clear reaches the shadows. The desktop's `RootCardinalPublisher::set` already deletes on gesture end; ensure WM restart, desktop crash and property loss clear safely. If temporary throttling/coalescing is needed, keep last-state-wins bounded to one native frame (not arbitrary 50–100ms delays); prioritize event coalescing and bounded rendering over hiding the problem behind a slow visible update rate.
>
> **Do not change the `_FLAMEWM_RUBBER` wire layout** unless the need is proven; any protocol changes must update both publisher, subscriber, API tests, and user-visible behavior in the same patch.
>
> ### 3. Eliminate the full-desktop paint per rubber movement in the DEFAULT X11 path
>
> **Owners:** `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/render.rs`, `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/damage_plan.rs` (only necessary localized functionality), `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/mod.rs`, `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/region_equivalence_tests.rs`; document integration `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/rubber.rs`, `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/main.rs`, `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/projection.rs` only if necessary. Preserve the public `UiDocumentAccess` semantics; `flamewm-ui-x11` remains the typed boundary.
>
> Implement a **desktop-only, default-on, single-purpose selection overlay fast path** with the following invariants:
>
> - Establish a proven stable backing scene/reference of what is underneath the rectangle. Retain server-side pixmaps (or use safe clipped command replay) and XRender compositing. For a pure geometry change, compute **exact changed pixels** of the old/new translucent fill and border, including borders that moved *within* the overlap. Rebuild/re-present **only these pixels**; do **not** take `bounding_box(old_rectangle, new_rectangle)` if that covers an unchanged interior.
> - Recomposition uses the **current** wallpaper, icon pixels, selected-icon highlights, notes and other desktop layers, never a stale screenshot taken once at drag start. When a tile changes selection state, invalidate/repaint that tile's precise old/new area and then apply the current selection overlay over it in correct Z order. A solid-cache fast path may be invalidated by icons, wallpaper/output changes, rename/menu appearance, popup movement, Expose, backend resize or scale; a safe full-frame redraw on those **infrequent unrelated events** is acceptable, but motion-only after settling must immediately resume the fast path.
> - Preserve the actual CSS-generated fill/border and alpha compositing. Avoid copying full wallpaper pixels to the X server each frame: `XCopyArea` (server-side pixmap copy) plus XRender fill/composite are preferable to `XPutImage` with per-motion large CPU buffers. Verify actual visual format, alpha mode and support on opaque/ARGB/shape fallback. The server's final visible pixels must match full redraws at the tested resolutions.
> - Reuse allocation/GC/picture/mask and buffers across frames, fixed-size rectangle arrays where possible. Surface resources are created once on demand and freed on shutdown/resize. Guard against extreme/off-screen dimensions/overflow.
> - Do not enable the generic opt-in region renderer globally: `FLAMEWM_RENDER_REGION=1` is documented as having regressions for terminal updates, clipped windows, text and overlays. Implement a **role-scoped fast path**, a narrow verified generalization, or a separate isolated compositor layer with explicit correctness tests. If the simplest fast solution is clipped replay, narrow dirty **strips** plus a retained command list and pixel-equivalent composite are acceptable. Global `Full` must remain the fallback for unsafe cases.
> - Preserve current pointer-event coalescing in `app/events.rs` and never coalesce across `ButtonRelease` or other semantic events. Press→motion→release, movement threshold, and hover/event delivery remain accurate.
> - `refresh_shape_mask_from_coverage_scaled` must not rebuild/re-submit an unchanged whole-screen XShape mask on every rubber step. Cache a semantic shape fingerprint/coverage when the opaque base already determines the shape. Do not skip genuine shape updates (transparent-only desktop, dock mask, dialogs, resizing, other UI roles).
>
> **Correctness architecture:** the desktop controller decides *selection state*, the renderer decides *damage/composition*, and the WM decides *shadows*. Do not move selection-hit semantics into X11 code or let UI directly manage windows. Prefer the smallest change implementing these responsibilities. The reference full-render pipeline must remain callable for fallback and test comparisons.
>
> ### 4. Regression tests and deterministic performance assertions
>
> Add or extend tests at the **actual owners**, not test-only alternative rendering:
>
> 1. `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/frame/shadow_rubber.rs`: exhaustive small-viewport property tests comparing the union of `dirty_regions(old,new)` against per-pixel `old_color != new_color`; if regions are conservatively padded, assert every changed pixel is covered and excess stays bounded. Include zero region on equal geometry; disjoint shadows; 1px, 2px, 1000px drags; color/alpha changes; fill↔border transitions; release; negative coordinates; all drag directions; edge clipping. Assert strip area is `O(perimeter × delta)` for a 1–2px move, never `O(rectangle area)` in those cases. Pixel compare `compose_region` patches versus full reference image for arbitrary overlaps.
> 2. `crates/flamewm-wm-x11/src/wm/shadow.rs` / reactor event tests: multiple queued PropertyNotify events lead to at most one property read/applied state per drained turn, preserve final clear, zero `PutImage` for disjoint regions, no `get_image`/server grab during drag, verify reused GC and cleanup.
> 3. `crates/flamewm-render-x11/src/app/region_equivalence_tests.rs`: adapt `selection_overlay_drag_full_vs_region_timing` and existing `compare_region_and_full` harness to use the **new DEFAULT desktop path**, not only `region_paint=true`. Compare screenshot bytes/pixels after **every** scripted step to authoritative full-frame path: begin below threshold, grow/shrink, move all corners, overlap icons, select/deselect, selected label/text shadows, right/bottom edges, transparency changes, notes/menus layered, Expose, resize, different scales, end/abort. Distinct random wallpaper/icons prevent false passes on blank surfaces. Test with compositing as used by FlameWM, and the fallback modes where supported.
> 4. `crates/flamewm-desktop/src/rubber.rs` / desktop event tests: preserve previously passing tests (`rubber_motion_matches_full_hit_test_and_toggles_only_changed_items`, `rubber_motion_does_not_project_cells_per_motion`, `root_rubber_payload_mirrors_overlay_rect_and_accent`) and guarantee no extra projection/hit changes during motion; output/work-area clamping and `selection_overlay` cleanup after release remain exact.
> 5. Counters: after warmup, hundreds of 1–2px pure rubber movements across a large rectangle must have `full_repaints=0`, `full_viewport_copy_pixels=0` and bounded changed/committed pixels. At rest: **zero** repeat paints, property changes, wakes from this feature or shadow uploads. During drag with no shadow overlap: `wm.rubber_put_image_calls=0`. Compare full visual output, not only decisions or execution times.
> 6. Integration under a dedicated nested display using `scripts/xephyr` + `FLAMEWM_TEST_DISPLAY` if available; exercise WM + desktop together. Test compositor on/off as supported. Repeat on native Xorg before declaring a laptop-level CPU improvement.
>
> Suggested scoped verification (adapt to the current repository toolchain and avoid concurrent builds):
>
> ```bash
> cargo fmt --all -- --check
> cargo test -p flamewm-api
> cargo test -p flamewm-wm-x11 shadow_rubber
> cargo test -p flamewm-desktop rubber
> cargo test -p flamewm-render-x11 region_paint_matches_full
> cargo test -p flamewm-render-core
> cargo test -p flamewm-ui-x11
> cargo build --release -p flamewm-wm-x11 -p flamewm-desktop -p flamewm-render-x11
> # Nested X11 integration: use the checked-in scripts/xephyr with an isolated bus.
> # Set FLAMEWM_TEST_DISPLAY to the *actual* nested display, never guess :0.
> ```
>
> If the current crate's target/filter does not match these examples, resolve the actual test name and record the exact command/result rather than claiming it passed.
>
> ### 5. Real-performance release criteria
>
> At minimum report a controlled table for the same before/after workload:
>
> | Metric | Before | After | Reduction |
> |---|---:|---:|---:|
> | Xorg or Xephyr CPU (% of one core) drag median and p95 | measured | measured | calculated |
> | FlameWM desktop CPU median/p95 | measured | measured | calculated |
> | WM CPU median/p95 | measured | measured | calculated |
> | Visible latency (p95 motion→present ms) | measured | measured | calculated |
> | Full desktop frames per 200 pure motions | measured | **0** after warmup | verified |
> | Shadow dirty/upload bytes for 200 motions | measured | measured | calculated |
> | Server-side copy / area touched per 200 motions | measured | measured | calculated |
> | Idle redraw/wakeup count over 10 s after release | measured | **0 feature-caused** | verified |
> | Pixel-equivalence failures (all fixtures) | measured | **0** | verified |
>
> **Optimization target:** reduce the incremental X-server CPU burden by **at least 80%** in an otherwise identical drag benchmark and aim for **90–95%+** where realistic, with no new lag or visual difference. These are **targets, not source-proven results**. If hardware, renderer fallback, or shadow count prevents meeting them, isolate the measured remaining owner and iterate; never manufacture a percentage or label a partial improvement complete.
>
> A strong implementation should make a large rectangle's **unchanged interior essentially free** while only the new edge bands and affected icon tiles cost work. Keep the input dispatch responsive even when mouse motion arrives faster than display refresh, avoiding unbounded queues. Frame limiting by itself does not solve server overdraw; use it only to drop obsolete visual states while preserving semantic press/release and final geometry.
>
> ## Boundaries / exclusions
>
> Do **not** alter Wayland, change desktop UX/appearance, disable shadow fidelity, downgrade transparency, introduce WebView/JS/WGPU, add per-motion image readbacks, introduce a separate continuously-refreshing compositor, weaken X11 input isolation, rewrite the general UI engine, change user data/settings formats, or touch unrelated features. Keep compatibility with X11 and existing fallback graphics modes. Inspect all affected callers, tests, fixtures, config/env, public exports, and resource teardown paths before editing. New build-time-only test fixtures and a bounded benchmark command are in scope.
>
> ## Final delivery required from the coding agent
>
> - Source patch/commit(s), with a minimal per-file change list and rationale; no synthetic code that bypasses the real path.
> - Tests executed and their results, including pixel-equivalence images/diffs and X11 fallback cases.
> - Measured **Xorg/Xephyr + WM + desktop** CPU and protocol/upload improvements on the same workload, with original logs and exact commands.
> - Any remaining unavoidable high-CPU path, untested hardware/graphics mode, or discrepancy against the 80% reduction target explicitly named. Do not claim 0% CPU during active drawing.
> - Confirm no regression to wallpaper, icon selection, menus, drag/releases, theme/opacity, stacking, shadows, and X11 session stability.
>
> ## Public protocol guidance checked
>
> - X.Org Xlib reference: `XCopyArea` and X server pixmap operations are native primitives; use server-side copies instead of downloading/reuploading static scene contents: https://xorg.freedesktop.org/archive/X11R7.6/doc/xorg-server/Xserver-spec.pdf
> - X.Org Xlib Expose semantics (do not assume visible window pixels survive exposure/occlusion): https://xorg.freedesktop.org/archive/current/doc/libX11/libX11/libX11.html
> - XRender rectangular composite/fills are standard primitives; verify exact premultiplied alpha and role fallback against current implementation: https://docs.rs/x11/latest/x11/xrender/fn.XRenderFillRectangles.html
> - X.Org protocol inter-client ordering is **not global** across X connections; never assume the desktop publisher's flush synchronizes the WM display: https://www.x.org/guide/extensions/
>
> **Completion definition:** visually indistinguishable desktop selection, bounded old/new-edge rendering and shadow damage, no full-screen redraw on motion, no per-event synchronous WM property storm, verified correctness and substantial measured reduction in the **actual X server's** CPU. Stop only when these outcomes are demonstrated or blockers are specifically documented.

1: //! Pure pseudo-transparency helpers for translucent shell surfaces (the taskbar).
2: //!
3: //! The snapshot is the root pixels under the bar, captured once before the bar is first mapped
4: //! (so the bar's own translucent pixels are never captured). It is static: it does not follow
5: //! wallpaper or window changes. Blur is applied from the stored snapshot, never recaptured.
6: 
7: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
8: 
9: use flamewm_api::background::WallpaperFit;
10: use flamewm_image_core::wallpaper::{self, DEFAULT_WALLPAPER_PATH};
11: use flamewm_image_core::RgbaImage;
12: pub use flamewm_ui_x11::backdrop::{blur_radius_px, MAX_BLUR_RADIUS_PX};
13: 
14: /// Fitted wallpaper pixels under `rect` (root-space device px): the wallpaper placed on the root
15: /// canvas exactly as the desktop owner does, computed for `rect` only. Pure: reads no root pixels,
16: /// so a bar's own paint or a not-yet-painted desktop cannot leak into the snapshot.
17: #[must_use]
18: pub fn wallpaper_backdrop(
19:     natural: &RgbaImage,
20:     root: (u32, u32),
21:     fit: WallpaperFit,
22:     rect: (i32, i32, u32, u32),
23: ) -> Option<RgbaImage> {
24:     wallpaper::compose_region(natural, root.0, root.1, fit, rect)
25: }
26: 
27: /// Fitted wallpaper pixels under `rect`, decoded from the `wallpaper` setting (empty means the
28: /// packaged default). `None` when the wallpaper is unavailable, so the caller falls back to a
29: /// root capture.
30: #[must_use]
31: pub fn wallpaper_source(
32:     wallpaper_setting: &str,
33:     fit: WallpaperFit,
34:     root: (u32, u32),
35:     rect: (i32, i32, u32, u32),
36:     packaged_root: &Path,
37: ) -> Option<RgbaImage> {
38:     let path = if wallpaper_setting.trim().is_empty() {
39:         packaged_root.join(DEFAULT_WALLPAPER_PATH)
40:     } else {
41:         PathBuf::from(wallpaper_setting)
42:     };
43:     match wallpaper::decode_file(&path) {
44:         Ok(natural) => wallpaper_backdrop(&natural, root, fit, rect),
45:         Err(error) => {
46:             backdrop_trace(format_args!(
47:                 "wallpaper source unavailable, root capture fallback: {error}"
48:             ));
49:             None
50:         }
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: /// Opaque ARGB32 words (0xFFRRGGBB) for the snapshot, blurred per [`blur_radius_px`].
55: #[must_use]
56: pub fn blurred_argb(snapshot: &RgbaImage, opacity_percent: u8, blur_percent: u8) -> Vec<u32> {
57:     flamewm_ui_x11::backdrop::blurred_argb_words(
58:         snapshot.width,
59:         snapshot.height,
60:         snapshot.pixels.clone(),
61:         opacity_percent,
62:         blur_percent,
63:     )
64: }
65: 
66: /// Debug trace for taskbar pseudo-transparency, enabled by `FLAMEWM_DEBUG_BACKDROP=1` (stderr).
67: pub fn backdrop_trace(message: std::fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
68:     static ENABLED: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
69:     if *ENABLED.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("FLAMEWM_DEBUG_BACKDROP").is_some_and(|v| v == "1"))
70:     {
71:         eprintln!("debug backdrop {message}");
72:     }
73: }

75: /// Captures attempted for one snapshot key before the bar stays solid.
76: pub const MAX_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS: u8 = 64;
77: 
78: /// What to do with a capture: install it, retry on the next refresh, or give up for this key.
79: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
80: pub enum CaptureStep {
81:     Use,
82:     Retry,
83:     GiveUp,
84: }
85: 
86: /// Decision after capture number `attempts_made` (1-based). A blank or uniform root is retried
87: /// until `MAX_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS`; the caller retries on its next event-driven refresh, never on a timer.
88: #[must_use]
89: pub fn capture_step(ready: bool, attempts_made: u8) -> CaptureStep {
90:     match (ready, attempts_made >= MAX_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS) {
91:         (true, _) => CaptureStep::Use,
92:         (false, false) => CaptureStep::Retry,
93:         (false, true) => CaptureStep::GiveUp,
94:     }
95: }
96: 
97: /// Inputs that change what the root looks like under the bar: wallpaper, its fit, and the bar rect.
98: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
99: pub struct CaptureKey {
100:     pub wallpaper: String,
101:     pub fit: String,
102:     pub rect: (i32, i32, u32, u32),
103: }

133:         unsafe {
134:             XTranslateCoordinates(self.display, self.window, root, 0, 0, &mut rx, &mut ry, &mut child)
135:         };

142:         else {
143:             return Ok(());
144:         };
145:         let key = MirrorKey {
146:             width,
147:             height,

150:                 i64::from(captured_root.1) - i64::from(ry),

152:         };
153:         let cached = self
154:             .window_backdrop
155:             .as_ref()
156:             .and_then(|s| s.mirror.as_ref())
157:             .filter(|fill| fill.key == key)
158:             .map(|fill| fill.pixmap);

160:             Some(pixmap) => pixmap,
161:             None => {

119: /// Pager columns, box and cell visibility for `cells`; no labels or fills.
120: ///
121: /// `workspace-column-j` is an absolutely positioned child of the pager, so
122: /// hidden columns consume no space and the visible ones keep the screen
123: /// positions of the box they replaced: column `j` (1-based) starts at
124: /// `cell_left(j - 1)` inside the pager content box.
125: fn project_pager_layout(
126:     document: &mut impl UiDocumentAccess,
127:     snapshot: Option<&flamewm_api::workspace::WorkspaceSnapshot>,
128:     cells: &[(usize, WorkspaceView)],
129: ) -> Result<(), String> {

131:     document.size("workspace-pager", pager_width(columns), PAGER_HEIGHT)?;
132:     for column in 0..PAGER_COLUMNS {
133:         let column_id = format!("workspace-column-{}", column + 1);
134:         if column < columns {
135:             document.position(&column_id, cell_left(column), 0.0)?;
136:             document.visible(&column_id, true)?;
137:         } else {
138:             document.visible(&column_id, false)?;
139:         }
140:     }
141:     for cell in 1..=PAGER_CELLS {
142:         document.visible(
143:             &format!("workspace-{cell}"),
144:             cells.iter().any(|(occupied, _)| *occupied == cell),
145:         )?;
146:     }
147:     Ok(())
148: }

69	pub fn solid_backdrop(color: (u8, u8, u8), rect: (i32, i32, u32, u32)) -> RgbaImage {
70	    let (_, _, width, height) = rect;
71	    let pixels = (width as usize)
72	        .saturating_mul(height as usize)
73	        .saturating_mul(4);
74	    RgbaImage {
75	        width,
76	        height,
77	        pixels: [color.0, color.1, color.2, 255]
78	            .repeat(pixels / 4),
79	    }
80	}

.task-button:hover, .task-slot:hover, .tray-button:hover, .clock:hover, .media-control:hover { background:var(--hover-fill); border-radius:8px; }
.task-button.disabled:hover, .task-slot.disabled:hover, .tray-button.disabled:hover, .clock.disabled:hover, .workspace-button.disabled:hover { background:transparent; }
.task-start-icon, .task-slot-icon { width:25px; height:25px; display:block; }
.task-button img { width:25px; height:25px; }
.task-slots { height:44px; display:flex; background:transparent; position:relative; }
.task-slot-insert { position:absolute; left:0px; top:6px; width:0px; height:0px; background:var(--accent); }
.task-slot { width:42px; height:44px; position:relative; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; background:transparent; color:var(--text); cursor:default; }.task-slot-label { position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:0px; height:0px; overflow:hidden; }
.task-slot .underline { background:transparent; }
.task-slot.running .underline { background:#87919b; }
.task-slot.focused .underline { left:5px; right:5px; width:auto; height:3px; background:var(--accent); }
.underline { position:absolute; left:7px; bottom:0px; width:28px; height:2px; }
.task-progress { position:absolute; left:7px; bottom:4px; height:2px; width:0px; background:var(--accent); }

Feature work is complete and the review session is live on **`:97`**.

**What's in this build:**
1. **Titlebars** toggle (default on). One authority point (`Wm::titlebar_height`), zero-band frame layout, resize edges stay 6px, controls/title-drag children unmap, and a live reflow so flipping it resizes open windows without a restart.
2. **Taskbar activities** toggle (default on). Off hides the running-window area, collapses its capsule/width, and the WM refuses minimize (`minimize()` early-returns) so windows can't become unreachable.
3. **Hyprland bindings**: `Super+Q` close, `Super+Return` terminal, `Super+1..9` workspaces, `Super+Shift+1..9` move to workspace, `Super+arrows` directional focus, `Super+Shift+arrows` move window, `Super+F` fullscreen, `Super+V` float/pseudo-tile, `Super+J/K` cycle, `Super+equal/minus` resize, `Super+M` minimize. The persisted-hotkey allowlist now covers all 56 actions instead of 8.
4. **Separate taskbar** (default on): start, activities, pager, tray group and clock each get their own 8px-rounded capsule — the same rounding as the hover highlight — with wallpaper visible in the gaps and no empty capsule when there are no windows.

**Transparency/blur fix:** the whole-bar frosted backdrop is gone in separate mode. The panel's surface layer is now the raw wallpaper (no tint, no blur), and each capsule gets `surfaceColor` + `surfaceOpacity` plus a per-node `surfaceBlurPercent` blur. In unified mode the single tinted/blurred bar is unchanged. A missing/unreadable wallpaper now falls back to `wallpaperColor` instead of compositing over a cleared black scene.

**Verification:** release build clean; 1,378 unit tests pass across api, platform, x11-desktop, wm-x11, shell and settings. Session logs show `install=true` and no backdrop/panic errors. I visually confirmed the capsules, gaps and titlebar on `:97` via screenshots.

Not verified yet: toggling titlebars/activities live from the Settings UI, and `Super`+mouse drag (not implemented — keyboard move works). Wayland hotkey dispatch wasn't extended, only X11.

The rubber-band/Xorg-CPU handoff is queued behind this. I'll hold until you've reviewed `:97` and given feedback, then start on it.
